function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Below is a quick‑start guide covering **where** you can get startup‑statistical data through existing APIs, **what kinds of metrics** those services expose, and a short example of how to hit one of those endpoints programmatically. --- ## 📌 What “Startup Stat” Usually Means | Metric | Typical Source | Example Use Case | |--------|-----------------|------------------| | Funding rounds & amounts | Crunchbase, Pitchbook, CB Insights | Track capital flow into sectors | | Valuation / exit multiples | Crunchbase, Pitchbook | Benchmark valuation trends | | Employee count & hiring pace | LinkedIn, Crunchbase | Gauge scaling speed | | Revenue & ARR estimates | PrivCo, Crunchbase, SaaS Capital | Forecast market size | | Geographic distribution | Crunchbase, AngelList | Identify hotbeds | | Product category tags | Crunchbase, AngelList | Segment startups by vertical | If your goal is *to create* an API yourself, you’ll usually scrape publicly available sources or use third‑party feeds and then wrap them behind your own REST interface. Below I list the most popular ready‑made APIs you can consume directly. --- ## 🔍 Top Public / Commercial Startup Stats APIs | Service | Free Tier | Key Features | Docs Link | |---------|-----------|--------------|------------| | **Crunchbase Pro API** | No – paid only | • All funding events
• Company profiles
• Investor networks | | | **AngelList API** | Yes (limited) | • Startups, jobs, investors
• Basic company metadata | | | **CB Insight’s API** | Paid | • Deal database
• Market reports | | | **PitchBook API** | Paid | • Private equity deals
• M&A activity | | | **Data.gov US Small Business Administration** | Free | • SBA loan data
• Grants | | | **OpenCorporates API** | Freemium | • Corporate filings worldwide | | | **Kaggle Datasets + API** | Free | • Pre‑compiled CSVs of funding, exits, etc. | | | **GitHub Repos (e.g., `startup-stats` projects)** | Free | • Community‑maintained scraped data | Search GitHub for “startup stats api” | ### Quick Comparison Table | Feature | Crunchbase | AngelList | CB Insights | PitchBook | OpenCorporates | |---------|-------------|----------|-------------|-----------|---------------| | Global coverage | ✔️ | ❓ | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | | Real‑time updates | ✔️ | ✖️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | | Pricing | $99+/mo | Limited free | Custom quotes | Custom quotes | Freemium | | Rate limits | 10k req/day | 100 req/min | Varies | Varies | 1k req/hr | --- ## 🛠 How To Call One Of These APIs Let’s walk through a simple example against the **AngelList** API because it has a generous free tier and requires almost nothing beyond a bearer token. ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://api.angel.co/1" def fetch_startup_by_name(name): """ Returns basic details for a startup found on AngelList. """ # Replace YOUR_TOKEN_HERE with your actual OAuth access token headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN_HERE}", "Accept": "application/json" } params = {"name": name} resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/companies", headers=headers, params=params) if resp.status_code != 200: raise Exception(f"Error {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}") return resp.json() if __name__ == "__main__": result = fetch_startup_by_name("Stripe") print(result["company"]["full_title"]) ``` #### Notes: - **Auth:** Most commercial APIs require OAuth tokens or API keys. For AngelList, generate a personal access token under Settings → Developer Apps. - **Rate Limits:** Respect the documented rate limit (`X-Ratelimit-Limit`, `Retry-After`) to avoid being throttled. - **Pagination:** Many endpoints paginate results—look for `_page` and `_per_page` query params. --- ## 🚀 Building Your Own Wrapper Suppose you decide to aggregate multiple sources into a single unified API. Here’s a minimal skeleton using Flask: ```python from flask import Flask, jsonify, request import requests app = Flask(__name__) CRUNCHBASE_API_KEY = "" ANGELLIST_ACCESS_TOKEN = "" @app.route("/stats/", methods=["GET"]) def get_stats(slug): # 1️⃣ Pull from Crunchbase cb_resp = requests.get( f"https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations/{slug}", params={"user_key": CRUNCHBASE_API_KEY}, ) cb_data = cb_resp.json() # 2️⃣ Pull from AngelList al_resp = requests.get( f"https://api.angel.co/1/companies/{slug}", headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {ANGELLIST_ACCESS_TOKEN}" }, ) al_data = al_resp.json() combined = { "crunchbase": cb_data, "angellist": al_data, } return jsonify(combined) if __name__ == "__main__": app.run(debug=True) ``` This tiny service now exposes `/stats/` where `` is the company slug used across both platforms. You can extend this pattern to include other providers, cache responses locally, add caching layers, or even run scheduled ETL jobs to keep data fresh. --- ## 🎯 When to Choose Which Provider? | Scenario | Recommended API | |----------|-----------------| | Need **funding history** + **valuation** | Crunchbase or PitchBook | | Want **publicly listed** startup data (US focus) | SEC EDGAR + S&P Capital IQ | | Looking for **global corporate registry** | OpenCorporates | | Interested in **job postings** + **talent pipeline** | AngelList Jobs | | Need **open source community** data | GitHub + Crunchbase (free tiers) | | Budget constraints | AngelList (free), OpenCorporates (freemium), Kaggle datasets | --- ## ⚙️ Next Steps 1. **Pick a provider** based on budget, geographic scope, and specific metrics you care about. 2. Sign up for an account/API key. 3. Read the docs carefully—especially pagination, filtering, and rate‑limit sections. 4. Write a small script to pull a handful of records and inspect the JSON schema. 5. Decide whether you’re happy consuming the raw feed or building a wrapper around it. Happy hacking—and may your startup insights grow faster than your portfolio!
